Navin's rules for this task (follow every one):
[G-01] Everything taught comes from the book. Knowledge from outside the book is allowed only to explain the book better; it is marked as outside, standard textbook-level and correct. Never invent facts, numbers, names or quotations.
[G-02] Work like the best teacher of these learners and this exam, not like a summariser. Depth beats brevity: nothing teachable on the page is skipped or compressed away, and every explanation makes a student understand, not just remember. Depth means understanding, not length: lesson narration keeps S2-01's time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-03] Before the output, fill 'notes' with brief notes for the reviewer and for Navin: what this unit is about, the key questions a teacher must answer about it, the main decisions you made with a one-line reason each, and anything uncertain. Keep the notes short; they explain the work, they are not the work.
[G-05] Never drop or compress away what the book teaches to fit a length. If a unit of work is too large, it is split by BIE into smaller units; within a unit, the book's content is complete. Lesson narration has a time target (S2-01), met by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-06] BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher (Navin, 24 October 2026). The book is the base; BIE carries its text, easy or hard, into the learner's mind. Never just read the line out: every book line is opened (what its words mean, why it is so, where it is seen, what follows), at the depth of the level profile.
[G-07] Two layers, like a film (Navin, 24 October 2026). The writer layer (understanding, plan, script) decides what is said and how deep, following the level profile and the book's own level. The presentation layer (director, video blocks, render) is the same skilled quality for every learner, from class 6 to postgraduate; only the detail shown follows the level, never the craft.
[S1-01] Read the page with two eyes: the native text blocks (exact words and numbers) and the page image (tables, diagrams, labels, arrows, equations, layout). Items that exist only in the image are as important as text items. A page whose text layer is empty or nearly empty is read entirely from the image.

A table continued from the previous page continues the same table.

BIE's content types (the type of an item decides its required questions and how it is taught, shown, played and drawn):
- process · Process: Something that happens in steps or stages over time: a mechanism, a procedure, a cycle (photosynthesis, cell division, how a bill becomes law). Required questions: how (kaise), when (kab). Other questions: what (kya), where (kahan), why (kyun), consequence (nateeja).
- structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).
- timeline · Timeline: Events placed in time: history, the development of an idea, stages of a life (the Revolt of 1857, evolution of cell theory). Required questions: when (kab), why (kyun). Other questions: who (kaun), where (kahan), consequence (nateeja).
- cause_effect · Reasoning (cause and effect): Why something happens: causes, effects, conditions and chains of reasoning (why tissues specialise, why prices rise, why a law was needed). Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).
- facts_numbers · Facts and numbers: Stated facts, quantities, measurements, statistics and formulas (heart rate 72 per minute, 3,000 against 50,000 soldiers at Plassey, F = ma). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: compare (tulna), why (kyun).
- figure · Figure: A diagram, photo, map, graph or table drawing on the page whose content is visual (tissue pages 2, 7 and 8 are figures only). Required questions: what (kya), which (kaun). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun).
- definition · Definition: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: about (kya), why (kyun).

How BIE talks to you: every request is a task card (JSON) followed by its source. The card names the unit, its parts with their content type and required questions, the ids of the rules above that apply, the output, the ids you must cover and the context. The card is BIE's instruction; the source is the material.
For a read_page card:
- card.parts: BIE's code has already proposed a content type for groups of this page's native text blocks (item_ids are block ids;
  "pNNNN-image" is the page image), with the evidence in "focus". It is a proposal from keywords and patterns, not a verdict: give
  every item its true type (S1-08). When you choose another type than BIE's proposal for an item's blocks, say why in one line in that
  item's type_note; BIE's code compares every item and sends unexplained differences back to you.
- card.coverage: every id in must_cover must be in some item's block_ids or in boilerplate_block_ids; may_skip lists blocks BIE thinks are
  running headers or page numbers. Never list an id that is not on this page.
- card.context.before and after: one line from the previous and the next page, for context only.
How to fill the JSON:
- notes: brief notes for the reviewer: what the page is about and how it fits the chapter, the key questions a teacher must answer,
  your main decisions (how you split items, how you read an unclear part, a type you chose against BIE's proposal) with a reason each,
  and what is uncertain.
- items: everything on the page, in reading order.
  - item_id: short and unique on this page ("i1", "i2", ...).
  - kind: heading, paragraph, definition, list_point, example, table (the whole table), table_row (one per row), diagram (the whole figure),
    diagram_label (one per label), equation, symbol, box_note, caption, question (a PYQ or practice question), answer_option, other.
  - parent_item_id: the table of a table_row, the diagram of a diagram_label, the question of an answer_option, else "". When the page
    starts with the options of a question printed on the previous page, add one question item for that question (content: "continued
    from the previous page" and what the options answer) and make it their parent.
  - source: "text" if the item comes from native text blocks, "image" if it is visible only in the image, "both" if both show it.
  - block_ids: the ids of the native text blocks this item covers ([] for image-only items). Use only ids from the card.
  - where_on_page: where it is ("top table, row 2", "right diagram, label at the axon end").
  - content: the exact words for text items; a complete, faithful reading for image items (every cell with its column header for a
    table_row; what a label names and what it points to for a diagram_label; all branches for a tree). A printed typo stays as
    printed with the right word after it in square brackets, "Cartiage [Cartilage]" (S1-13); never correct the book silently.
  - content_type: one of BIE's nine type ids above, by what the content is. An example takes the type of what it illustrates; a table
    row or a diagram label usually takes its table's or diagram's type. "none" only for a question, an answer option or an item that is
    not teachable.
  - type_note: "" when you agree with BIE's proposal for this item's blocks (or there is none); otherwise one line on why your type fits.
  - teachable: false only for pure headings and containers whose children carry the content.
  - teacher_understanding: the teacher's questions and answers for this item (S1-06); depth 1 for first questions, 2 and more for
    "why"/"how" on an earlier answer; basis "book" only if the page states it, else "outside"; one answer, one basis: an answer that
    would mix what the book says with an outside explanation becomes two answers, one "book" and one "outside" (S1-14). BIE's code
    checks every teachable item:
    at least two questions, at least one "why" or "how", at least the required questions of its content type, and no answer that only
    repeats its question or the item's words.
  - prerequisites: concrete concepts a student must understand first.
  - exam_importance and exam_note: for this exam.
  - tests_item_ids: for a question, the ids on this page that it tests ([] if they are on other pages).
  - unpack: how a teacher opens this book line for the learner (S1-15; BIE is the link between the learner and the book, never a
    reader of the line). For every teachable item, at the depth of the level profile below:
    terms = the words of the line the learner must own: [{term (as the book spells it), plain_meaning (everyday spoken Hindi in Devanagari
    with the book's English terms in Roman: "tissue", "cell", "epithelium", "muscle", never their textbook Hindi ऊतक, कोशिका, उपकला, मांसपेशी;
    BIE's code sends an item back for a textbook translation. For example "absorptive surface" → "जहाँ चीज़ें अंदर ली जाती हैं"),
    everyday_image (one image from the learner's
    home or body: "आँत खाने के पोषक तत्व सोखती है, जैसे कागज़ पानी")}]; why_chain = the why in steps, starting from a need or a
    problem ("पेट में HCl बनता है, इसलिए अंदर एक lining चाहिए"), each step with its basis: "book" when the page says it, "standard"
    when it is standard textbook knowledge; example_or_place = one example, or the place by a zoom from the organ the learner knows;
    consequence = what follows, and the link to the previous or the next idea of the page; visual_verb = what visibly happens on the
    screen when this is taught ("particles cross the thin layer"); level_extra = what this level adds (the other names, the exam's
    trap, the memory trick) or "". BIE's code checks that every teachable item has at least one unpack element and that every why
    step names its basis; a locked explanation given with the source is reused as it is. A question item or a pure heading leaves
    unpack empty.
- boilerplate_block_ids: ids of running headers, page numbers, adverts, contact lines and watermarks only.

Level profile: UPSC / State PCS (level_profiles.json; learners: UPSC and State PCS aspirants, often from arts backgrounds, who need understanding more than technical vocabulary).
- Terms: fewer technical terms: only the ones the exam asks, each opened with its plain meaning and an everyday image; a term the exam never asks is explained in words, not named.
- Why: 2 step(s); a two-step why from a need the learner can feel, then its link to daily life, health or governance.
- Where found: the main places, each linked to something the learner already knows (a disease, a food, a news item).
- Exam beats: the PYQ pattern: how this fact has been asked (statement combinations, 'which is correct', odd one out) and the wording that traps.
- Links: daily life, health, the news and earlier chapters of the same paper.

How real teachers open a book line (teacher example bank 2026-10-24.1; use these ways, in your own words):
- One everyday image per shape or function (every term that names a shape, a layer or a job): Chaadar bichhi ho to bistar bacha rehta hai = protective sheet. Cube wala game, har side barabar = cuboidal. Building ka pillar = columnar. Farsh ki tiles = squamous, isliye tessellated bhi kehte hain.
- The word root where it helps (a term whose parts carry its meaning): Epi yaani upar; epithelium yaani upar ki parat. Slender yaani long aur narrow.
- Why starts from a need (every why step): Pet mein HCl banta hai, isliye andar ek lining chahiye jo khud na jale. Cells bahar ki taraf hain, tootne ka chance zyada, isliye regeneration zyada.
- Link to something already known (a new place or a new structure): Peritoneum, jaise lungs ke aas-paas pleura aur heart ke aas-paas pericardium: wahi kaam, pet ke andar.
- Meaning with two or three real examples (an abstract word in the book): Sensory perception yaani pehchanna: thanda lagna, dard hona, pressure mehsoos karna.
- Open the book's adjective (Navin's example) (a book line names a kind of surface, job or place without saying what it is): Book: 'epithelium absorptive aur secretive surfaces par milta hai'. Teacher: absorptive surface yaani jahan cheezein andar li jaati hain, jaise aant khane ke poshak tatva sokhti hai; secretive yaani jahan cells kuch bana kar bahar chhodte hain, jaise glands enzyme ya juice. Aur epithelium wahan kyon? Kyunki ek patli, lagi hui parat hi cheezon ko paar jaane de sakti hai aur bana kar chhod sakti hai.

items.content: Phloem is made up of five types of cells: sieve cells, sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem fibres and the phloem parenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: Which five components does the book include in phloem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sieve cells, sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem fibres and phloem parenchyma form the book's five-part list.

teacher_understanding.question: How do these components differ in their main roles?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sieve elements conduct food; companion cells assist sieve tubes; parenchyma stores materials; fibres provide support. Sieve cells and sieve tubes represent different kinds of conducting elements, not a compulsory pair in every plant.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does a conducting tissue contain several cell types?
teacher_understanding.answer: Moving food needs conducting passages, living support and storage, while the plant also needs reinforcement; different cells share these tasks.

items.exam_note: Learn the component list and avoid assuming every listed type occurs together in every plant.

terms.plain_meaning: पौधे में बना खाना पहुँचाने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: रसोई से अलग-अलग कमरों तक खाना पहुँचाने की व्यवस्था

why_chain.step: Leaves make food, but other parts also need it.
Phloem combines conducting and supporting cell types to serve that need.

unpack.consequence: A complex tissue is not a collection of identical cells.
unpack.visual_verb: separate and colour-code five components
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish a general component list from universal co-occurrence.

items.content: Sieve tubes are tubular cells with perforated walls.

teacher_understanding.question: What do tubular and perforated mean here?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tubular means elongated like a pipe; perforated means having openings rather than forming an uninterrupted barrier.

teacher_understanding.question: Where are sieve tubes located?
teacher_understanding.answer: They are included among the cell types of phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: How do perforations help transport?
teacher_understanding.answer: Openings in sieve plates between neighbouring sieve-tube elements allow food-containing sap to pass along the conducting pathway.

items.exam_note: Connect perforated sieve plates with food conduction.

terms.plain_meaning: ऐसी दीवारें जिनमें छोटे रास्ते या छेद हों
terms.everyday_image: छन्नी में छेद होते हैं जिनसे चीज़ें पार जा सकती हैं

why_chain.step: Food sap must pass between successive conducting cells.
Perforated end walls provide connecting openings.

unpack.consequence: Shape and wall openings support conduction.
unpack.visual_verb: pass sap through perforated end plates
unpack.level_extra: Do not interpret this as holes throughout every wall.

items.content: Phloem transports food from leaves to other parts of the plant.
items.type_note: This states a transport function, not the spatial arrangement of plant parts.

teacher_understanding.question: What material does phloem distribute?
teacher_understanding.answer: It carries food from leaves to other plant parts.

teacher_understanding.question: What else on this page reinforces that function?
teacher_understanding.answer: The comparison table says phloem carries food materials from leaves to growing parts.

teacher_understanding.question: Why must food leave the leaves?
teacher_understanding.answer: Roots, developing shoots and other consuming or storage regions need sugars even when they do not make enough themselves.

items.exam_note: Food transport is the key contrast with xylem; do not infer exclusively downward transport.

terms.plain_meaning: बना हुआ खाना दूसरी जगह पहुँचाता है
terms.everyday_image: रसोई का खाना खाने वालों तक पहुँचाना

why_chain.step: Non-photosynthetic and growing regions require food.
Phloem carries food from leaves to other parts.

unpack.consequence: Food production and food use can occur in different places.
unpack.visual_verb: send food arrows from a leaf to growing regions
unpack.level_extra: Source-to-sink transport can occur in different directions in different tubes.

items.content: Comparison table with columns S.No., Xylem and Phloem; six rows compare transported material, living/dead cells, wall thickness, permeability, wall material and mechanical strength.
items.exam_note: Six statement-based comparison criteria.

items.content: S.No.: 1. | Xylem: It carries water and minerals from roots to leaves. | Phloem: It carries food materials from the leaves to the growing parts of the plant.

teacher_understanding.question: What transport contrast does the row make?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem supplies water and minerals from roots towards leaves; phloem supplies food from leaves to growing regions.

teacher_understanding.question: How do the transported materials differ?
teacher_understanding.answer: Water and mineral ions are not the manufactured sugars carried in food sap.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are separate transport functions useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: Roots obtain water and minerals while photosynthetic leaves manufacture sugars; the plant must connect these different supply points with regions of demand.

items.exam_note: Common reversal trap: water/minerals versus food.

terms.plain_meaning: जड़ों से पानी और minerals पहुँचाने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: पानी ऊपर पहुँचाने वाली पाइप

why_chain.step: Leaves need root-supplied water and growing parts need leaf-made food.
Xylem and phloem serve these distinct supply needs.

unpack.consequence: Identify tissue by cargo, not merely arrow direction.
unpack.visual_verb: contrast water arrows with food arrows
unpack.level_extra: Phloem is not defined as downward-only.

items.content: S.No.: 2. | Xylem: It is composed of dead cells. | Phloem: It is composed of living cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What broad contrast does the book present?
teacher_understanding.answer: The table associates xylem with dead cells and phloem with living cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What qualification prevents an incorrect absolute statement?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem parenchyma is living; phloem fibres are generally dead. The contrast describes the dominant conducting-cell condition rather than every component.

teacher_understanding.question: How can dead cells conduct water?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mature vessel elements and tracheids retain wall-bounded spaces that allow water passage without living cell contents.

items.exam_note: High-value exceptions: xylem parenchyma and phloem fibres.

terms.plain_meaning: जिनमें जीवित अंदरूनी हिस्सा नहीं बचा
terms.everyday_image: खाली पाइप की दीवार बनी रहती है

why_chain.step: Water requires a continuous conducting route.
Dead mature xylem conducting elements retain passages; living phloem participates in food transport.

unpack.consequence: Avoid converting a broad contrast into an all-cell rule.
unpack.visual_verb: empty a xylem lumen and highlight living phloem
unpack.level_extra: Apply the explicit phloem-fibre exception below the table.

items.content: S.No.: 3. | Xylem: It has a thick cell wall. | Phloem: It has a thin cell wall.

teacher_understanding.question: What wall-thickness contrast is printed?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem is described as thick-walled and phloem as thin-walled.

teacher_understanding.question: How should this contrast be applied?
teacher_understanding.answer: It principally contrasts conducting elements; phloem fibres have thick walls, so it is not universal across every component.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are strong xylem walls useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: They help conducting passages resist collapse under water tension and reinforce the plant.

items.exam_note: Remember thick-walled phloem fibres as a qualification.

terms.plain_meaning: cell के चारों ओर मोटी मजबूत दीवार
terms.everyday_image: पतली नली की जगह मजबूत पाइप

why_chain.step: Water-conducting passages must resist collapse.
Thick reinforced walls help preserve their shape.

unpack.consequence: Wall thickness links transport with support.
unpack.visual_verb: thicken the xylem wall
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish conducting elements from fibres.

items.content: S.No.: 4. | Xylem: Its cells are impermeable to the water. | Phloem: Its cells are permeable to food components.

teacher_understanding.question: Which permeability contrast does the table state?
teacher_understanding.answer: It describes xylem cells as impermeable to water and phloem cells as permeable to food components.

teacher_understanding.question: Why must this wording not be read as a complete transport explanation?
teacher_understanding.answer: Water travels through xylem lumens and passes between elements through pits or perforations. Lignified walls do not mean that xylem as a pathway blocks water; phloem transfer is also regulated rather than unrestricted leakage.

teacher_understanding.question: How can a reinforced tube carry water despite resistant walls?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its hollow interior provides a route along the tube; wall properties and passage along the lumen are different issues.

items.exam_note: Potentially misleading wording: distinguish wall resistance from water conduction.

terms.plain_meaning: जिसके आर-पार आसानी से न जा सके
terms.everyday_image: पाइप की दीवार पानी रोकती है, भीतर का रास्ता पानी ले जाता है

why_chain.step: A transport passage must carry material without being confused with its side wall.
Xylem water passage uses lumens and connecting openings.

unpack.consequence: Do not conclude that xylem prevents water transport.
unpack.visual_verb: separate across-wall movement from along-tube movement
unpack.level_extra: Flag this as a simplified textbook contrast.

items.content: S.No.: 5. | Xylem: Its cells are made up of lignin. | Phloem: Its cells are made up of cellulose.

teacher_understanding.question: Which materials does the book contrast?
teacher_understanding.answer: It associates xylem with lignin and phloem with cellulose.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the accurate distinction behind this shorthand?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem conducting-element walls are reinforced with lignin as well as containing cellulose; cellulose is not exclusive to phloem. The cells themselves are not made solely of one of these substances.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does lignin matter?
teacher_understanding.answer: Lignin stiffens walls and makes them more resistant to collapse, supporting both conduction and mechanical strength.

items.exam_note: Lignification, not exclusive possession of cellulose, is the meaningful contrast.

terms.plain_meaning: दीवार को कड़ा और मजबूत बनाने वाला पदार्थ
terms.everyday_image: लकड़ी की सख्ती

terms.plain_meaning: plant cell की दीवार का मुख्य ढाँचा बनाने वाला पदार्थ
terms.everyday_image: कपास के रेशे

why_chain.step: Water-conducting walls need reinforcement.
Lignin strengthens their cellulose-containing walls.

unpack.consequence: Wall composition helps explain thickness and support.
unpack.visual_verb: reinforce a cellulose wall with lignin
unpack.level_extra: Reject 'xylem contains no cellulose'.

items.content: S.No.: 6. | Xylem: It gives mechanical strength to the plants. | Phloem: Phloem does not give mechanical strength

teacher_understanding.question: What support contrast is printed?
teacher_understanding.answer: The table assigns mechanical strength to xylem and denies it to phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: What exception qualifies the phloem statement?
teacher_understanding.answer: Phloem fibres provide mechanical support, so the printed denial should not be applied to every phloem component.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does xylem reinforce a plant?
teacher_understanding.answer: Thick lignified walls resist deformation and act as structural reinforcement.

items.exam_note: Phloem fibres are the important qualification to the absolute wording.

terms.plain_meaning: भार और झुकाव सहकर आकार बनाए रखने की ताकत
terms.everyday_image: इमारत का मजबूत ढाँचा

why_chain.step: A plant must remain upright while carrying leaves and branches.
Reinforced xylem and supporting fibres help bear those loads.

unpack.consequence: Transport tissue can also have a supporting role.
unpack.visual_verb: brace an upright stem
unpack.level_extra: Avoid the absolute claim that no phloem component supports.

items.content: A stem segment labels epidermis, cortex, pith, cambium, xylem and phloem. A red curved arrow enlarges a vascular region into a longitudinal view: xylem at left, cambium in the middle, phloem at right. Black arrows rise within xylem; the illustrated phloem arrows descend. Xylem shows elongated tubes with wall thickening and open connections; phloem shows stacked conducting elements with perforated end regions and adjacent narrow cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What relationship does the enlargement show?
teacher_understanding.answer: The red arrow connects the stem's vascular region to a magnified view of xylem, cambium and phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which directions are drawn?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem arrows point upward and the phloem arrows shown point downward.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the phloem arrows be interpreted?
teacher_understanding.answer: They depict one transport direction, not a universal restriction. Phloem carries material from a source to a sink, which may lie above or below it.

items.exam_note: Identify inner xylem, intervening cambium and outer phloem.

terms.plain_meaning: xylem और phloem के बीच नई cells बनाने वाली परत
terms.everyday_image: दो हिस्सों के बीच नई ईंटें जोड़ने वाली पट्टी

why_chain.step: A small vascular region is difficult to distinguish in the whole stem.
The enlarged view separates its conducting and growing regions.

unpack.example_or_place: The stem shown beside the table.
unpack.consequence: Spatial arrangement can be linked with transport function.
unpack.visual_verb: zoom into the vascular region and animate arrows
unpack.level_extra: The red arrow means enlargement, not sap movement.

items.content: epidermis — points to the outer surface layer of the stem.

teacher_understanding.question: What does epidermis identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: The outer covering of the small stem drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: Which labelled region lies farther inward?
teacher_understanding.answer: The cortex lies beneath the epidermis.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is an outer covering useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: It protects internal tissues and helps limit unwanted water loss.

items.exam_note: Recognise the outermost labelled layer.

terms.plain_meaning: सबसे बाहर की ढकने वाली परत
terms.everyday_image: फल का बाहरी छिलका

unpack.consequence: Locates the boundary before moving inward.
unpack.visual_verb: outline the outer layer

items.content: cortex — points to tissue beneath the epidermis and outside the vascular region.

teacher_understanding.question: What region is labelled cortex?
teacher_understanding.answer: The peripheral tissue inside the stem's outer covering.

teacher_understanding.question: Which position distinguishes it from pith?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cortex is toward the outside of the vascular tissues; pith occupies the central region.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this help read the diagram?
teacher_understanding.answer: It provides an outer landmark for locating the deeper vascular tissues.

items.exam_note: Use cortex as an outer positional landmark.

terms.plain_meaning: बाहरी परत के नीचे का हिस्सा
terms.everyday_image: छिलके के अंदर की पट्टी

unpack.consequence: Separates outer tissue from central pith.
unpack.visual_verb: shade the peripheral band

items.content: pith — points to the central internal region of the stem.

teacher_understanding.question: What does pith name in this drawing?
teacher_understanding.answer: The stem's central internal region.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue is nearer the pith: xylem or phloem?
teacher_understanding.answer: In this arrangement, xylem lies on the inner side toward the pith.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the pith label orient the learner?
teacher_understanding.answer: It establishes the centre, allowing inner xylem to be distinguished from outer phloem.

items.exam_note: Central landmark, not a conducting-tissue label.

terms.plain_meaning: तने के बीच का अंदरूनी हिस्सा
terms.everyday_image: गोल चीज़ का बीच वाला भाग

unpack.consequence: Helps orient the vascular arrangement.
unpack.visual_verb: highlight the centre

items.content: cambium — points to the layer between xylem and phloem in the vascular region.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this cambium label locate?
teacher_understanding.answer: The intervening region between the two conducting tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: Which meristem category includes vascular cambium?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is a lateral meristem associated with secondary growth.

teacher_understanding.question: How does it increase stem girth?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its divisions produce secondary xylem inward and secondary phloem outward.

items.exam_note: Links the diagram with lateral meristem in the practice question.

terms.plain_meaning: नई cells बनाकर मोटाई बढ़ाने वाली परत
terms.everyday_image: दीवार में नई कतारें जोड़ना

unpack.consequence: Connects tissue location with growth in girth.
unpack.visual_verb: add cells to both sides
unpack.level_extra: Vascular cambium is a lateral meristem.

items.content: xylem — points to the inner conducting region of the small stem.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this xylem label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: The inner conducting region selected for enlargement.

teacher_understanding.question: Which cargo belongs to this tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: The table assigns water and minerals to xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: How can it be distinguished spatially from phloem?
teacher_understanding.answer: In this stem arrangement, it lies inward of cambium while phloem is outward.

items.exam_note: Combine position and cargo.

terms.plain_meaning: पानी और minerals ले जाने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: भीतर की पानी वाली पाइप

unpack.example_or_place: Inner side of the vascular region.
unpack.consequence: Connects the whole stem with the enlargement.
unpack.visual_verb: trace xylem into the enlarged view

items.content: phloem — points to the outer conducting region of the small stem.

teacher_understanding.question: What region does this phloem label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: The outer conducting region shown beside the xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which transported material identifies phloem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Food from leaves is assigned to phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: How does location help distinguish it?
teacher_understanding.answer: In this arrangement, phloem lies outside cambium rather than toward the pith.

items.exam_note: Outer phloem versus inner xylem.

terms.plain_meaning: बना खाना पहुँचाने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: खाना पहुँचाने का रास्ता

unpack.consequence: Identifies the food-conducting side.
unpack.visual_verb: trace phloem into the enlargement

items.content: xylem — brackets the left-hand thickened conducting tubes with upward arrows.

teacher_understanding.question: What structures are grouped under xylem?
teacher_understanding.answer: The enlarged left-hand elongated conducting structures.

teacher_understanding.question: Which direction is shown within them?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their black arrows point upward.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the wall pattern relate to function?
teacher_understanding.answer: Wall reinforcement helps maintain open water-conducting passages.

items.exam_note: Identify xylem from thickened walls and upward water pathway.

why_chain.step: Water pathways must remain open.
Reinforced walls resist collapse.

unpack.consequence: Links microscopic structure with table contrasts.
unpack.visual_verb: raise water arrows through tubes

items.content: cambium — brackets the narrow central cell region separating xylem and phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the enlarged cambium label group?
teacher_understanding.answer: The narrow central region between the two conducting tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissues border it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem borders its left side and phloem its right side in the enlargement.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is this location significant?
teacher_understanding.answer: A dividing layer here can add vascular tissue to both sides during secondary growth.

items.exam_note: Recognise cambium by its intervening position.

why_chain.step: A thickening stem needs additional conducting tissue.
Cambium adds xylem and phloem on opposite sides.

unpack.consequence: Explains the lateral-growth connection.
unpack.visual_verb: expand the central strip into new rows

items.content: phloem — brackets the right-hand conducting region with perforated end regions and downward arrows.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the enlarged phloem label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: The right-hand food-conducting region adjacent to cambium.

teacher_understanding.question: Which visible feature connects with the sieve-tube bullet?
teacher_understanding.answer: The conducting elements show perforated end regions.

teacher_understanding.question: How should its downward arrows be taught?
teacher_understanding.answer: As the illustrated direction of food movement, not proof that phloem transport is exclusively downward.

items.exam_note: Arrow direction is illustrative, not an absolute rule.

why_chain.step: Food must pass between adjoining conducting elements.
Perforated sieve plates provide connecting routes.

unpack.consequence: Connects sieve-tube structure with food movement.
unpack.visual_verb: pass food through sieve plates
unpack.level_extra: Source and sink determine direction.

items.content: Except phloem fibres, other phloem cells are living cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Which phloem component is the stated exception?
teacher_understanding.answer: Phloem fibres are excluded from the statement that phloem cells are living.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this line qualify the table?
teacher_understanding.answer: It explicitly adds an exception to the table's broad description of phloem as composed of living cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can fibres function after losing living contents?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their supporting role depends mainly on strong walls rather than continuing metabolism.

items.exam_note: Classic exception and odd-one-out fact.

terms.plain_meaning: phloem के मजबूत सहारा देने वाले लंबे हिस्से
terms.everyday_image: रस्सी के मजबूत रेशे

why_chain.step: A plant needs structural support as well as food movement.
Fibre walls can provide support without living contents at maturity.

unpack.consequence: The word 'all' makes a living-phloem statement unsafe.
unpack.visual_verb: single out the fibre from living components
unpack.level_extra: Living sieve-tube elements lack a nucleus at maturity; absence of a nucleus alone does not mean dead.

items.content: Q. Fat present below the skin surface in our body, acts as a barrier against: (HPAS 2020)
items.type_note: 2020 identifies the examination year; this is a biological function question, not a timeline.

teacher_understanding.question: Which option answers the question?
teacher_understanding.answer: Option a, loss of heat from our body.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does fat beneath skin reduce heat loss?
teacher_understanding.answer: Adipose tissue conducts heat poorly and adds insulation between warmer internal tissues and the cooler surroundings.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is the microorganism option a trap?
teacher_understanding.answer: The skin's surface barrier chiefly limits entry of microorganisms; the question specifically asks about fat beneath it.

items.exam_note: HPAS 2020: match subcutaneous fat with thermal insulation.

items.content: a. Loss of heat from our body

teacher_understanding.question: Why is this the correct choice?
teacher_understanding.answer: Subcutaneous fat acts as thermal insulation, reducing transfer of body heat to the surroundings.

teacher_understanding.question: How does insulation differ from producing heat?
teacher_understanding.answer: It slows heat escape rather than directly creating the heat being conserved.

items.exam_note: Correct option; distinguish conservation from generation.

terms.plain_meaning: शरीर की गरमी बाहर निकलना
terms.everyday_image: कंबल गरमी बाहर जाने की रफ्तार घटाता है

why_chain.step: Body heat can escape into cooler surroundings.
Fat slows heat transfer and helps conserve warmth.

unpack.consequence: Supports temperature maintenance.
unpack.visual_verb: slow outward heat arrows
unpack.level_extra: Correct: a.

items.content: b. Loss of essential body nutrients

teacher_understanding.question: What confusion does this distractor invite?
teacher_understanding.answer: It confuses fat's role as an energy store with acting as a barrier against nutrient loss.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is it not the best answer?
teacher_understanding.answer: The insulating function of subcutaneous fat directly concerns heat transfer, not a general blockade against nutrients leaving the body.

items.exam_note: Storage is not the barrier function asked here.

unpack.consequence: Reject a related but mismatched function.
unpack.visual_verb: separate storage from insulation

items.content: c. Loss of salts from the body

teacher_understanding.question: What loss does this option propose?
teacher_understanding.answer: It proposes salt loss rather than heat loss as the process blocked by fat.

teacher_understanding.question: Why should it be rejected?
teacher_understanding.answer: Salt balance involves processes such as kidney regulation and sweating; subcutaneous fat is not the relevant salt-retention barrier.

items.exam_note: Do not confuse thermal insulation with salt balance.

unpack.consequence: Separate heat transfer from loss of dissolved substances.
unpack.visual_verb: contrast heat arrows and sweat droplets

items.content: d. Entry of harmful micro-organisms from the environments

teacher_understanding.question: Which protection is described by this option?
teacher_understanding.answer: Protection against entry of harmful microorganisms from outside the body.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is this not the answer for fat below skin?
teacher_understanding.answer: The intact skin surface is the main physical barrier at this interface; underlying fat is being tested for insulation.

items.exam_note: The phrase 'below the skin' distinguishes fat from the surface barrier.

terms.plain_meaning: बहुत छोटे जीव, जिन्हें देखने के लिए अक्सर microscope चाहिए
terms.everyday_image: घाव में infection करने वाले germs

unpack.example_or_place: Intact skin versus a skin wound.
unpack.consequence: Assign the correct function to the correct layer.
unpack.visual_verb: stop germs at the skin surface

items.content: PRACTICE QUESTIONS
Q. Consider the following statements: Choose the correct statement(s):

teacher_understanding.question: Which printed statements are correct?
teacher_understanding.answer: Statements 2 and 3 are correct in the standard textbook treatment; statement 1 is incorrect.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does statement 1 fail?
teacher_understanding.answer: Apical meristems occur at shoot tips as well as root tips, so 'root tips only' is too restrictive.

teacher_understanding.question: How should this combination question be solved?
teacher_understanding.answer: Check each tissue-location pairing independently and scrutinise restrictive words before selecting the combination.

items.exam_note: Correct combination: 2 and 3; answer choices are not on this page.

items.content: Tissue | Location. Three numbered statements pair Apical, Lateral and Intercalary tissues with locations.
items.exam_note: These are propositions to evaluate, not an answer-key table.

items.content: 1. Tissue: Apical | Location: Present at root tips only

teacher_understanding.question: How does the printed location compare with the correct one?
teacher_understanding.answer: The printed statement restricts apical tissue to root tips; apical meristems also occur at shoot tips.

teacher_understanding.question: What word changes this from acceptable to incorrect?
teacher_understanding.answer: 'Only' excludes shoot tips and makes the statement false.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are growing tips associated with apical meristems?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cell division there supplies new cells for primary growth, helping roots and shoots extend in length.

items.exam_note: Statement 1 is false because of 'only'.

terms.everyday_image: टहनी का बढ़ता हुआ सिरा

why_chain.step: Roots and shoots need to extend into new space.
Apical meristems provide new cells at both kinds of tip.

unpack.consequence: A true example becomes false when made exclusive.
unpack.visual_verb: highlight both root and shoot tips
unpack.level_extra: Statement-combination trap: 'only'.

items.content: 2. Tissue: Lateral | Location: Present beneath bark

teacher_understanding.question: How does lateral-meristem location compare with apical location?
teacher_understanding.answer: Lateral meristems occur along the sides of stems and roots, rather than being confined to their growing tips.

teacher_understanding.question: How does their growth effect differ?
teacher_understanding.answer: Lateral meristems increase girth; apical meristems chiefly contribute to primary length growth.

teacher_understanding.question: How is the printed statement understood?
teacher_understanding.answer: The beneath-bark location is accepted in this school-level pairing; vascular and cork cambia are examples of lateral meristems associated with thickening.

items.exam_note: Statement 2 is correct in the intended textbook context.

terms.plain_meaning: किनारों या बगल की तरफ मौजूद
terms.everyday_image: तने की मोटाई बढ़ती हुई देखना

why_chain.step: An enlarging plant needs a thicker stem and additional tissues.
Lateral meristems add cells that increase girth.

unpack.consequence: Links the practice statement with the vascular diagram.
unpack.visual_verb: widen the stem outward
unpack.level_extra: Contrast length growth with girth growth.

items.content: 3. Tissue: Intercalary | Location: Present at base of leaves or internodes

teacher_understanding.question: How does intercalary location differ from apical location?
teacher_understanding.answer: Intercalary meristems lie between more mature regions, commonly at leaf bases or internode bases, rather than at the terminal tip.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this differ from lateral meristems?
teacher_understanding.answer: Intercalary growth helps extend particular leaf or stem regions; lateral meristems chiefly increase girth.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this location explain familiar regrowth?
teacher_understanding.answer: In grasses, basal growing regions can remain after upper portions are cut or grazed, permitting continued growth.

items.exam_note: Statement 3 is correct; associate intercalary meristems with grasses.

terms.plain_meaning: बड़े हो चुके हिस्सों के बीच बचा बढ़ने वाला भाग

Basal intercalary regions supply new cells for that extension.

unpack.consequence: Location explains continued growth after grazing or cutting.

output.page_summary: Phloem components, sieve-tube structure and food transport; six xylem–phloem contrasts; a labelled vascular-tissue diagram; and questions on insulation by fat and meristem locations.

items.content: Phloem is made up of five types of cells: sieve cells, sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem fibres and the phloem parenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: Which five components does the book include in phloem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sieve cells, sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem fibres and phloem parenchyma form the book's five-part list.

teacher_understanding.question: How do these components differ in their main roles?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sieve elements conduct food; companion cells assist sieve tubes; parenchyma stores materials; fibres provide support. Sieve cells and sieve tubes represent different kinds of conducting elements, not a compulsory pair in every plant.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does a conducting tissue contain several cell types?
teacher_understanding.answer: Moving food needs conducting passages, living support and storage, while the plant also needs reinforcement; different cells share these tasks.

items.exam_note: Learn the component list and avoid assuming every listed type occurs together in every plant.

terms.plain_meaning: पौधे में बना खाना पहुँचाने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: रसोई से अलग-अलग कमरों तक खाना पहुँचाने की व्यवस्था

why_chain.step: Leaves make food, but other parts also need it.
Phloem combines conducting and supporting cell types to serve that need.

unpack.consequence: A complex tissue is not a collection of identical cells.
unpack.visual_verb: separate and colour-code five components
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish a general component list from universal co-occurrence.

items.content: Sieve tubes are tubular cells with perforated walls.

teacher_understanding.question: What do tubular and perforated mean here?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tubular means elongated like a pipe; perforated means having openings rather than forming an uninterrupted barrier.

teacher_understanding.question: Where are sieve tubes located?
teacher_understanding.answer: They are included among the cell types of phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: How do perforations help transport?
teacher_understanding.answer: Openings in sieve plates between neighbouring sieve-tube elements allow food-containing sap to pass along the conducting pathway.

items.exam_note: Connect perforated sieve plates with food conduction.

terms.plain_meaning: ऐसी दीवारें जिनमें छोटे रास्ते या छेद हों
terms.everyday_image: छन्नी में छेद होते हैं जिनसे चीज़ें पार जा सकती हैं

why_chain.step: Food sap must pass between successive conducting cells.
Perforated end walls provide connecting openings.

unpack.consequence: Shape and wall openings support conduction.
unpack.visual_verb: pass sap through perforated end plates
unpack.level_extra: Do not interpret this as holes throughout every wall.

items.content: Phloem transports food from leaves to other parts of the plant.
items.type_note: This states a transport function, not the spatial arrangement of plant parts.

teacher_understanding.question: What material does phloem distribute?
teacher_understanding.answer: It carries food from leaves to other plant parts.

teacher_understanding.question: What else on this page reinforces that function?
teacher_understanding.answer: The comparison table says phloem carries food materials from leaves to growing parts.

teacher_understanding.question: Why must food leave the leaves?
teacher_understanding.answer: Roots, developing shoots and other consuming or storage regions need sugars even when they do not make enough themselves.

items.exam_note: Food transport is the key contrast with xylem; do not infer exclusively downward transport.

terms.plain_meaning: बना हुआ खाना दूसरी जगह पहुँचाता है
terms.everyday_image: रसोई का खाना खाने वालों तक पहुँचाना

why_chain.step: Non-photosynthetic and growing regions require food.
Phloem carries food from leaves to other parts.

unpack.consequence: Food production and food use can occur in different places.
unpack.visual_verb: send food arrows from a leaf to growing regions
unpack.level_extra: Source-to-sink transport can occur in different directions in different tubes.

items.content: Comparison table with columns S.No., Xylem and Phloem; six rows compare transported material, living/dead cells, wall thickness, permeability, wall material and mechanical strength.
items.exam_note: Six statement-based comparison criteria.

items.content: S.No.: 1. | Xylem: It carries water and minerals from roots to leaves. | Phloem: It carries food materials from the leaves to the growing parts of the plant.

teacher_understanding.question: What transport contrast does the row make?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem supplies water and minerals from roots towards leaves; phloem supplies food from leaves to growing regions.

teacher_understanding.question: How do the transported materials differ?
teacher_understanding.answer: Water and mineral ions are not the manufactured sugars carried in food sap.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are separate transport functions useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: Roots obtain water and minerals while photosynthetic leaves manufacture sugars; the plant must connect these different supply points with regions of demand.

items.exam_note: Common reversal trap: water/minerals versus food.

terms.plain_meaning: जड़ों से पानी और minerals पहुँचाने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: पानी ऊपर पहुँचाने वाली पाइप

why_chain.step: Leaves need root-supplied water and growing parts need leaf-made food.
Xylem and phloem serve these distinct supply needs.

unpack.consequence: Identify tissue by cargo, not merely arrow direction.
unpack.visual_verb: contrast water arrows with food arrows
unpack.level_extra: Phloem is not defined as downward-only.

items.content: S.No.: 2. | Xylem: It is composed of dead cells. | Phloem: It is composed of living cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What broad contrast does the book present?
teacher_understanding.answer: The table associates xylem with dead cells and phloem with living cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What qualification prevents an incorrect absolute statement?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem parenchyma is living; phloem fibres are generally dead. The contrast describes the dominant conducting-cell condition rather than every component.

teacher_understanding.question: How can dead cells conduct water?
teacher_understanding.answer: Mature vessel elements and tracheids retain wall-bounded spaces that allow water passage without living cell contents.

items.exam_note: High-value exceptions: xylem parenchyma and phloem fibres.

terms.plain_meaning: जिनमें जीवित अंदरूनी हिस्सा नहीं बचा
terms.everyday_image: खाली पाइप की दीवार बनी रहती है

why_chain.step: Water requires a continuous conducting route.
Dead mature xylem conducting elements retain passages; living phloem participates in food transport.

unpack.consequence: Avoid converting a broad contrast into an all-cell rule.
unpack.visual_verb: empty a xylem lumen and highlight living phloem
unpack.level_extra: Apply the explicit phloem-fibre exception below the table.

items.content: S.No.: 3. | Xylem: It has a thick cell wall. | Phloem: It has a thin cell wall.

teacher_understanding.question: What wall-thickness contrast is printed?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem is described as thick-walled and phloem as thin-walled.

teacher_understanding.question: How should this contrast be applied?
teacher_understanding.answer: It principally contrasts conducting elements; phloem fibres have thick walls, so it is not universal across every component.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are strong xylem walls useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: They help conducting passages resist collapse under water tension and reinforce the plant.

items.exam_note: Remember thick-walled phloem fibres as a qualification.

terms.plain_meaning: cell के चारों ओर मोटी मजबूत दीवार
terms.everyday_image: पतली नली की जगह मजबूत पाइप

why_chain.step: Water-conducting passages must resist collapse.
Thick reinforced walls help preserve their shape.

unpack.consequence: Wall thickness links transport with support.
unpack.visual_verb: thicken the xylem wall
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish conducting elements from fibres.

items.content: S.No.: 4. | Xylem: Its cells are impermeable to the water. | Phloem: Its cells are permeable to food components.

teacher_understanding.question: Which permeability contrast does the table state?
teacher_understanding.answer: It describes xylem cells as impermeable to water and phloem cells as permeable to food components.

teacher_understanding.question: Why must this wording not be read as a complete transport explanation?
teacher_understanding.answer: Water travels through xylem lumens and passes between elements through pits or perforations. Lignified walls do not mean that xylem as a pathway blocks water; phloem transfer is also regulated rather than unrestricted leakage.

teacher_understanding.question: How can a reinforced tube carry water despite resistant walls?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its hollow interior provides a route along the tube; wall properties and passage along the lumen are different issues.

items.exam_note: Potentially misleading wording: distinguish wall resistance from water conduction.

terms.plain_meaning: जिसके आर-पार आसानी से न जा सके
terms.everyday_image: पाइप की दीवार पानी रोकती है, भीतर का रास्ता पानी ले जाता है

why_chain.step: A transport passage must carry material without being confused with its side wall.
Xylem water passage uses lumens and connecting openings.

unpack.consequence: Do not conclude that xylem prevents water transport.
unpack.visual_verb: separate across-wall movement from along-tube movement
unpack.level_extra: Flag this as a simplified textbook contrast.

items.content: S.No.: 5. | Xylem: Its cells are made up of lignin. | Phloem: Its cells are made up of cellulose.

teacher_understanding.question: Which materials does the book contrast?
teacher_understanding.answer: It associates xylem with lignin and phloem with cellulose.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the accurate distinction behind this shorthand?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem conducting-element walls are reinforced with lignin as well as containing cellulose; cellulose is not exclusive to phloem. The cells themselves are not made solely of one of these substances.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does lignin matter?
teacher_understanding.answer: Lignin stiffens walls and makes them more resistant to collapse, supporting both conduction and mechanical strength.

items.exam_note: Lignification, not exclusive possession of cellulose, is the meaningful contrast.

terms.everyday_image: लकड़ी की सख्ती

terms.plain_meaning: plant cell की दीवार का मुख्य ढाँचा बनाने वाला substance
terms.everyday_image: कपास के रेशे

why_chain.step: Water-conducting walls need reinforcement.
Lignin strengthens their cellulose-containing walls.

unpack.consequence: Wall composition helps explain thickness and support.
unpack.visual_verb: reinforce a cellulose wall with lignin
unpack.level_extra: Reject 'xylem contains no cellulose'.

items.content: S.No.: 6. | Xylem: It gives mechanical strength to the plants. | Phloem: Phloem does not give mechanical strength

teacher_understanding.question: What support contrast is printed?
teacher_understanding.answer: The table assigns mechanical strength to xylem and denies it to phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: What exception qualifies the phloem statement?
teacher_understanding.answer: Phloem fibres provide mechanical support, so the printed denial should not be applied to every phloem component.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does xylem reinforce a plant?
teacher_understanding.answer: Thick lignified walls resist deformation and act as structural reinforcement.

items.exam_note: Phloem fibres are the important qualification to the absolute wording.

terms.plain_meaning: भार और झुकाव सहकर आकार बनाए रखने की ताकत
terms.everyday_image: इमारत का मजबूत ढाँचा

why_chain.step: A plant must remain upright while carrying leaves and branches.
Reinforced xylem and supporting fibres help bear those loads.

unpack.consequence: Transport tissue can also have a supporting role.
unpack.visual_verb: brace an upright stem
unpack.level_extra: Avoid the absolute claim that no phloem component supports.

items.content: A stem segment labels epidermis, cortex, pith, cambium, xylem and phloem. A red curved arrow enlarges a vascular region into a longitudinal view: xylem at left, cambium in the middle, phloem at right. Black arrows rise within xylem; the illustrated phloem arrows descend. Xylem shows elongated tubes with wall thickening and open connections; phloem shows stacked conducting elements with perforated end regions and adjacent narrow cells.

teacher_understanding.question: What relationship does the enlargement show?
teacher_understanding.answer: The red arrow connects the stem's vascular region to a magnified view of xylem, cambium and phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: Which directions are drawn?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem arrows point upward and the phloem arrows shown point downward.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the phloem arrows be interpreted?
teacher_understanding.answer: They depict one transport direction, not a universal restriction. Phloem carries material from a source to a sink, which may lie above or below it.

items.exam_note: Identify inner xylem, intervening cambium and outer phloem.

terms.plain_meaning: xylem और phloem के बीच नई cells बनाने वाली परत
terms.everyday_image: दो हिस्सों के बीच नई ईंटें जोड़ने वाली पट्टी

why_chain.step: A small vascular region is difficult to distinguish in the whole stem.
The enlarged view separates its conducting and growing regions.

unpack.example_or_place: The stem shown beside the table.
unpack.consequence: Spatial arrangement can be linked with transport function.
unpack.visual_verb: zoom into the vascular region and animate arrows
unpack.level_extra: The red arrow means enlargement, not sap movement.

items.content: epidermis — points to the outer surface layer of the stem.

teacher_understanding.question: What does epidermis identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: The outer covering of the small stem drawing.

teacher_understanding.question: Which labelled region lies farther inward?
teacher_understanding.answer: The cortex lies beneath the epidermis.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is an outer covering useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: It protects internal tissues and helps limit unwanted water loss.

items.exam_note: Recognise the outermost labelled layer.

terms.plain_meaning: सबसे बाहर की ढकने वाली परत
terms.everyday_image: फल का बाहरी छिलका

unpack.consequence: Locates the boundary before moving inward.
unpack.visual_verb: outline the outer layer

items.content: cortex — points to tissue beneath the epidermis and outside the vascular region.

teacher_understanding.question: What region is labelled cortex?
teacher_understanding.answer: The peripheral tissue inside the stem's outer covering.

teacher_understanding.question: Which position distinguishes it from pith?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cortex is toward the outside of the vascular tissues; pith occupies the central region.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this help read the diagram?
teacher_understanding.answer: It provides an outer landmark for locating the deeper vascular tissues.

items.exam_note: Use cortex as an outer positional landmark.

terms.plain_meaning: बाहरी परत के नीचे का हिस्सा
terms.everyday_image: छिलके के अंदर की पट्टी

unpack.visual_verb: shade the peripheral band

items.content: pith — points to the central internal region of the stem.

teacher_understanding.question: What does pith name in this drawing?
teacher_understanding.answer: The stem's central internal region.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue is nearer the pith: xylem or phloem?
teacher_understanding.answer: In this arrangement, xylem lies on the inner side toward the pith.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the pith label orient the learner?
teacher_understanding.answer: It establishes the centre, allowing inner xylem to be distinguished from outer phloem.

items.exam_note: Central landmark, not a conducting-tissue label.

terms.plain_meaning: तने के बीच का अंदरूनी हिस्सा
terms.everyday_image: गोल चीज़ का बीच वाला भाग

unpack.consequence: Helps orient the vascular arrangement.

items.content: cambium — points to the layer between xylem and phloem in the vascular region.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this cambium label locate?
teacher_understanding.answer: The intervening region between the two conducting tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: Which meristem category includes vascular cambium?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is a lateral meristem associated with secondary growth.

teacher_understanding.question: How does it increase stem girth?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its divisions produce secondary xylem inward and secondary phloem outward.

items.exam_note: Links the diagram with lateral meristem in the practice question.

terms.plain_meaning: नई cells बनाकर मोटाई बढ़ाने वाली परत
terms.everyday_image: दीवार में नई कतारें जोड़ना

unpack.consequence: Connects tissue location with growth in girth.
unpack.visual_verb: add cells to both sides
unpack.level_extra: Vascular cambium is a lateral meristem.

items.content: xylem — points to the inner conducting region of the small stem.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this xylem label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: The inner conducting region selected for enlargement.

teacher_understanding.question: Which cargo belongs to this tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: The table assigns water and minerals to xylem.

teacher_understanding.question: How can it be distinguished spatially from phloem?
teacher_understanding.answer: In this stem arrangement, it lies inward of cambium while phloem is outward.

items.exam_note: Combine position and cargo.

terms.plain_meaning: पानी और minerals ले जाने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: भीतर की पानी वाली पाइप

unpack.consequence: Connects the whole stem with the enlargement.
unpack.visual_verb: trace xylem into the enlarged view

items.content: phloem — points to the outer conducting region of the small stem.

teacher_understanding.answer: The outer conducting region shown beside the xylem.

teacher_understanding.answer: Food from leaves is assigned to phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: How does location help distinguish it?
teacher_understanding.answer: In this arrangement, phloem lies outside cambium rather than toward the pith.

items.exam_note: Outer phloem versus inner xylem.

items.content: xylem — brackets the left-hand thickened conducting tubes with upward arrows.

teacher_understanding.question: What structures are grouped under xylem?
teacher_understanding.answer: The enlarged left-hand elongated conducting structures.

teacher_understanding.question: Which direction is shown within them?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their black arrows point upward.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the wall pattern relate to function?
teacher_understanding.answer: Wall reinforcement helps maintain open water-conducting passages.

items.exam_note: Identify xylem from thickened walls and upward water pathway.

why_chain.step: Water pathways must remain open.
Reinforced walls resist collapse.

unpack.consequence: Links microscopic structure with table contrasts.
unpack.visual_verb: raise water arrows through tubes

items.content: cambium — brackets the narrow central cell region separating xylem and phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the enlarged cambium label group?
teacher_understanding.answer: The narrow central region between the two conducting tissues.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissues border it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem borders its left side and phloem its right side in the enlargement.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is this location significant?
teacher_understanding.answer: A dividing layer here can add vascular tissue to both sides during secondary growth.

items.exam_note: Recognise cambium by its intervening position.

why_chain.step: A thickening stem needs additional conducting tissue.
Cambium adds xylem and phloem on opposite sides.

unpack.consequence: Explains the lateral-growth connection.
unpack.visual_verb: expand the central strip into new rows

items.content: phloem — brackets the right-hand conducting region with perforated end regions and downward arrows.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the enlarged phloem label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: The right-hand food-conducting region adjacent to cambium.

teacher_understanding.question: Which visible feature connects with the sieve-tube bullet?
teacher_understanding.answer: The conducting elements show perforated end regions.

teacher_understanding.question: How should its downward arrows be taught?
teacher_understanding.answer: As the illustrated direction of food movement, not proof that phloem transport is exclusively downward.

items.exam_note: Arrow direction is illustrative, not an absolute rule.

why_chain.step: Food must pass between adjoining conducting elements.
Perforated sieve plates provide connecting routes.

unpack.consequence: Connects sieve-tube structure with food movement.
unpack.visual_verb: pass food through sieve plates
unpack.level_extra: Source and sink determine direction.

items.content: Except phloem fibres, other phloem cells are living cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Which phloem component is the stated exception?
teacher_understanding.answer: Phloem fibres are excluded from the statement that phloem cells are living.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this line qualify the table?
teacher_understanding.answer: It explicitly adds an exception to the table's broad description of phloem as composed of living cells.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can fibres function after losing living contents?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their supporting role depends mainly on strong walls rather than continuing metabolism.

items.exam_note: Classic exception and odd-one-out fact.

terms.plain_meaning: phloem के मजबूत सहारा देने वाले लंबे हिस्से
terms.everyday_image: रस्सी के मजबूत रेशे

why_chain.step: A plant needs structural support as well as food movement.
Fibre walls can provide support without living contents at maturity.

unpack.consequence: The word 'all' makes a living-phloem statement unsafe.
unpack.visual_verb: single out the fibre from living components
unpack.level_extra: Living sieve-tube elements lack a nucleus at maturity; absence of a nucleus alone does not mean dead.

items.content: Q. Fat present below the skin surface in our body, acts as a barrier against: (HPAS 2020)
items.type_note: 2020 identifies the examination year; this is a biological function question, not a timeline.

teacher_understanding.question: Which option answers the question?
teacher_understanding.answer: Option a, loss of heat from our body.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does fat beneath skin reduce heat loss?
teacher_understanding.answer: Adipose tissue conducts heat poorly and adds insulation between warmer internal tissues and the cooler surroundings.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is the microorganism option a trap?
teacher_understanding.answer: The skin's surface barrier chiefly limits entry of microorganisms; the question specifically asks about fat beneath it.

items.exam_note: HPAS 2020: match subcutaneous fat with thermal insulation.

items.content: a. Loss of heat from our body

teacher_understanding.question: Why is this the correct choice?
teacher_understanding.answer: Subcutaneous fat acts as thermal insulation, reducing transfer of body heat to the surroundings.

teacher_understanding.question: How does insulation differ from producing heat?
teacher_understanding.answer: It slows heat escape rather than directly creating the heat being conserved.

items.exam_note: Correct option; distinguish conservation from generation.

terms.plain_meaning: शरीर की गरमी बाहर निकलना
terms.everyday_image: कंबल गरमी बाहर जाने की रफ्तार घटाता है

why_chain.step: Body heat can escape into cooler surroundings.
Fat slows heat transfer and helps conserve warmth.

unpack.consequence: Supports temperature maintenance.
unpack.visual_verb: slow outward heat arrows
unpack.level_extra: Correct: a.

items.content: b. Loss of essential body nutrients

teacher_understanding.question: What confusion does this distractor invite?
teacher_understanding.answer: It confuses fat's role as an energy store with acting as a barrier against nutrient loss.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is it not the best answer?
teacher_understanding.answer: The insulating function of subcutaneous fat directly concerns heat transfer, not a general blockade against nutrients leaving the body.

items.exam_note: Storage is not the barrier function asked here.

unpack.consequence: Reject a related but mismatched function.
unpack.visual_verb: separate storage from insulation

items.content: c. Loss of salts from the body

teacher_understanding.question: What loss does this option propose?
teacher_understanding.answer: It proposes salt loss rather than heat loss as the process blocked by fat.

teacher_understanding.question: Why should it be rejected?
teacher_understanding.answer: Salt balance involves processes such as kidney regulation and sweating; subcutaneous fat is not the relevant salt-retention barrier.

items.exam_note: Do not confuse thermal insulation with salt balance.

unpack.consequence: Separate heat transfer from loss of dissolved substances.
unpack.visual_verb: contrast heat arrows and sweat droplets

items.content: d. Entry of harmful micro-organisms from the environments

teacher_understanding.question: Which protection is described by this option?
teacher_understanding.answer: Protection against entry of harmful microorganisms from outside the body.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is this not the answer for fat below skin?
teacher_understanding.answer: The intact skin surface is the main physical barrier at this interface; underlying fat is being tested for insulation.

items.exam_note: The phrase 'below the skin' distinguishes fat from the surface barrier.

terms.plain_meaning: बहुत छोटे जीव, जिन्हें देखने के लिए अक्सर microscope चाहिए
terms.everyday_image: घाव में infection करने वाले germs

unpack.example_or_place: Intact skin versus a skin wound.
unpack.consequence: Assign the correct function to the correct layer.
unpack.visual_verb: stop germs at the skin surface

items.content: PRACTICE QUESTIONS
Q. Consider the following statements: Choose the correct statement(s):

teacher_understanding.question: Which printed statements are correct?
teacher_understanding.answer: Statements 2 and 3 are correct in the standard textbook treatment; statement 1 is incorrect.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does statement 1 fail?
teacher_understanding.answer: Apical meristems occur at shoot tips as well as root tips, so 'root tips only' is too restrictive.

teacher_understanding.question: How should this combination question be solved?
teacher_understanding.answer: Check each tissue-location pairing independently and scrutinise restrictive words before selecting the combination.

items.exam_note: Correct combination: 2 and 3; answer choices are not on this page.

items.content: Tissue | Location. Three numbered statements pair Apical, Lateral and Intercalary tissues with locations.
items.exam_note: These are propositions to evaluate, not an answer-key table.

items.content: 1. Tissue: Apical | Location: Present at root tips only

teacher_understanding.question: How does the printed location compare with the correct one?
teacher_understanding.answer: The printed statement restricts apical tissue to root tips; apical meristems also occur at shoot tips.

teacher_understanding.question: What word changes this from acceptable to incorrect?
teacher_understanding.answer: 'Only' excludes shoot tips and makes the statement false.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are growing tips associated with apical meristems?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cell division there supplies new cells for primary growth, helping roots and shoots extend in length.

items.exam_note: Statement 1 is false because of 'only'.

terms.plain_meaning: सिरे पर मौजूद
terms.everyday_image: टहनी का बढ़ता हुआ सिरा

why_chain.step: Roots and shoots need to extend into new space.
Apical meristems provide new cells at both kinds of tip.

unpack.consequence: A true example becomes false when made exclusive.
unpack.visual_verb: highlight both root and shoot tips
unpack.level_extra: Statement-combination trap: 'only'.

items.content: 2. Tissue: Lateral | Location: Present beneath bark

teacher_understanding.question: How does lateral-meristem location compare with apical location?
teacher_understanding.answer: Lateral meristems occur along the sides of stems and roots, rather than being confined to their growing tips.

teacher_understanding.question: How does their growth effect differ?
teacher_understanding.answer: Lateral meristems increase girth; apical meristems chiefly contribute to primary length growth.

teacher_understanding.question: How is the printed statement understood?
teacher_understanding.answer: The beneath-bark location is accepted in this school-level pairing; vascular and cork cambia are examples of lateral meristems associated with thickening.

items.exam_note: Statement 2 is correct in the intended textbook context.

terms.plain_meaning: किनारों या बगल की तरफ मौजूद
terms.everyday_image: तने की मोटाई बढ़ती हुई देखना

why_chain.step: An enlarging plant needs a thicker stem and additional tissues.
Lateral meristems add cells that increase girth.

unpack.consequence: Links the practice statement with the vascular diagram.
unpack.visual_verb: widen the stem outward
unpack.level_extra: Contrast length growth with girth growth.

items.content: 3. Tissue: Intercalary | Location: Present at base of leaves or internodes

teacher_understanding.question: How does intercalary location differ from apical location?
teacher_understanding.answer: Intercalary meristems lie between more mature regions, commonly at leaf bases or internode bases, rather than at the terminal tip.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this differ from lateral meristems?
teacher_understanding.answer: Intercalary growth helps extend particular leaf or stem regions; lateral meristems chiefly increase girth.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this location explain familiar regrowth?
teacher_understanding.answer: In grasses, basal growing regions can remain after upper portions are cut or grazed, permitting continued growth.

items.exam_note: Statement 3 is correct; associate intercalary meristems with grasses.

terms.plain_meaning: बड़े हो चुके हिस्सों के बीच बचा बढ़ने वाला भाग
terms.everyday_image: घास कटने के बाद नीचे से फिर बढ़ती है

terms.plain_meaning: तने में दो nodes के बीच का हिस्सा
terms.everyday_image: बाँस की दो गाँठों के बीच का भाग

why_chain.step: A leaf or stem segment may need to keep extending away from the terminal tip.
Basal intercalary regions supply new cells for that extension.

unpack.example_or_place: Leaf bases and internode bases in grasses.
unpack.consequence: Location explains continued growth after grazing or cutting.
unpack.visual_verb: extend grass upward from its base
unpack.level_extra: Do not confuse intercalary length growth with lateral thickening.
